p.src: Now Cao Ren, consumed with rage, mustered all the troops under his command and crossed the river by night, intent on razing Xinye to the ground.

u.src: Now Cao Ren, consumed with rage, mustered all the troops under his command and crossed the river by night, intent on razing Xinye to the ground.

p.src: Meanwhile, Shan Fu returned victorious to the county town and told Xuande, “Cao Ren is encamped at Fancheng. When he learns that his two commanders have been slain, he is certain to bring a great army against us.” Xuande asked, “How should we meet him?” Shan Fu replied, “If he brings all his troops here, Fancheng will be left undefended, and we can seize the opportunity to make a surprise attack.” Xuande asked him for a plan. Shan Fu leaned close and whispered the details in his ear. Xuande was delighted, and all preparations were made in advance. Suddenly a scout reported, “Cao Ren is crossing the river with a great army!” Shan Fu said, “Just as I expected.” He then asked Xuande to lead out the army and meet the enemy. When the two armies had drawn up opposite each other, Zhao Yun rode forth and called for an opposing commander to parley. Cao Ren ordered Li Dian into the field, and he engaged Zhao Yun. After exchanging some dozen bouts, Li Dian realized he was no match for his opponent, wheeled his horse, and returned to his lines. Zhao Yun spurred after him, but archers on both wings checked his pursuit; thereupon both sides withdrew to their camps.

p.src: Li Dian returned to Cao Ren and said, “Their troops are elite. We must not underestimate them. We would do better to return to Fancheng.” Cao Ren flew into a rage. “Before we even marched, you were already weakening our army’s spirit; now you have disgraced us in battle as well. Your crime deserves beheading!” He shouted for the executioners to drag Li Dian away and behead him. Only the other commanders’ earnest pleas saved him. Cao Ren assigned Li Dian to command the rear division and personally led the vanguard. The next day he advanced to the beat of drums, deployed his forces in a formation, and sent a man to ask Xuande, “Do you recognize my formation?”

p.src: Shan Fu climbed to high ground and surveyed it, then said to Xuande, “This is the Eight-Gate Golden Locks Formation. Its eight gates are Rest, Life, Injury, Obstruction, Prospect, Death, Alarm, and Opening. Entering by the Gates of Life, Prospect, or Opening brings good fortune; entering by the Gates of Injury, Alarm, or Rest brings wounds; and entering by the Gates of Obstruction or Death brings destruction. Although the eight gates have been arrayed neatly, the center still lacks proper direction. If we strike through the Gate of Life at the southeastern corner and emerge through the Gate of Prospect due west, the formation is certain to collapse into disorder.”

p.src: Xuande issued his orders, directing his soldiers to hold the corners of the formation and commanding Zhao Yun to lead five hundred men in from the southeast and drive straight out to the west. Receiving the order, Zhao Yun leveled his spear, leapt onto his horse, and led his men with a great shout against the southeastern corner, cutting his way into the central division. Cao Ren fled northward. Zhao Yun did not pursue him, but burst through the western gate, then wheeled around and fought his way back to the southeastern corner. Cao Ren’s army was thrown into utter confusion. Xuande waved his army forward in a charge, and Cao Cao’s troops were soundly defeated and driven back. Shan Fu ordered them not to pursue, and the army was recalled.

p.src: After Cao Ren had lost this battle, he finally believed Li Dian’s warning; he called Li Dian back to confer and said, “There must be a capable strategist in Liu Bei’s army, for my formation was completely broken.” Li Dian said, “Though I am here, I am deeply worried about Fancheng.” Cao Ren said, “Tonight we shall raid their camp. If we win, we can decide our next move afterward; if we do not, we shall withdraw to Fancheng.” Li Dian said, “You must not. Liu Bei is certain to be prepared.” Cao Ren said, “If one harbors so many doubts, how can one wage war?” Thus he refused to heed Li Dian’s advice. He personally led the vanguard, ordered Li Dian to support him from the rear, and set out to raid the camp during the second watch that night.

p.src: Meanwhile, as Shan Fu and Xuande were discussing affairs in the camp, a fierce wind suddenly sprang up. Shan Fu said, “Cao Ren is certain to raid our camp tonight.” Xuande asked, “How shall we oppose him?” Shan Fu smiled. “I have already calculated everything.” He then secretly completed all the necessary deployments. At the second watch, as Cao Ren’s troops drew near the camp, flames suddenly rose on every side within it and caught the stockade fences. Cao Ren realized preparations had been made and urgently ordered a retreat. Zhao Yun came charging down upon them. Unable to rally his troops and return to camp, Cao Ren hastily fled toward the river to the north. Just as he reached the riverbank and was seeking boats to cross, a fierce body of troops charged along the shore, led by none other than Zhang Fei. Cao Ren fought desperately while Li Dian protected him until he boarded a boat and crossed the river. More than half of Cao Cao’s army drowned in the river.

p.src: After crossing the river, Cao Ren came ashore and raced to Fancheng, where he ordered his men to call for the gate to be opened. Suddenly a drum sounded atop the walls, and a commander led troops out, shouting, “I took Fancheng long ago!” They looked in alarm and saw that it was Guan Yunchang. Cao Ren was aghast and immediately wheeled his horse to flee. Yunchang came pursuing and striking down his men. Cao Ren lost many more men and horses, then fled through the night toward Xuchang. From inquiries along the road, he finally learned that Shan Fu was serving as military adviser and had devised the entire strategy.

p.src: We shall say no more of Cao Ren’s defeated return to Xuchang. Meanwhile, Xuande had won a complete victory and led his army into Fancheng, where Liu Mi, the county magistrate, came out to welcome him. Xuande restored order among the people. Liu Mi was a native of Changsha and likewise a kinsman of the imperial house. He invited Xuande to his home and entertained him with a banquet. Xuande noticed a man standing in attendance nearby. Seeing his imposing and distinguished bearing, he asked Liu Mi, “Who is this man?” Liu Mi replied, “This is my nephew, Kou Feng, the son of the Kou family of the Marquis of Luo. Since both his parents died, he has been living here under my care.” Xuande took a liking to him and wished to adopt him as his son. Liu Mi gladly consented, and Kou Feng bowed to Xuande as his father and changed his name to Liu Feng. Xuande took him back and instructed him to bow to Yunchang and Yide as his uncles. Yunchang said, “Elder brother, since you already have a son, why adopt another? He is certain to cause trouble in the future.” Xuande replied, “If I treat him as a son, he will surely serve me as a father. What trouble could there be?” Yunchang was displeased. After consulting Shan Fu, Xuande ordered Zhao Yun to guard Fancheng with one thousand troops. Xuande then led the rest back to Xinye.

p.src: Meanwhile, Cao Ren and Li Dian returned to the capital of Xu and appeared before Cao Cao. Weeping, they bowed to the ground and begged forgiveness, recounting in full how they had lost commanders and troops. Cao Cao said, “Victory and defeat are the common lot of soldiers. But who devised Liu Bei’s strategy?” Cao Ren replied that it was Shan Fu’s plan. Cao Cao asked, “Who is Shan Fu?” Cheng Yu laughed. “That man is not Shan Fu. From youth he was fond of learning and swordsmanship. Toward the end of the Zhongping era, he once killed a man to avenge another. He let down his hair, smeared his face, and fled, but was captured by the officers. When questioned, he refused to give his name. The officers therefore bound him to a cart and paraded him through the marketplace to the beat of drums, calling on the townspeople to identify him; yet even those who knew him dared not speak. His companions secretly rescued him, whereupon he changed his name and fled. He abandoned his former ways, devoted himself to study, and sought instruction from renowned teachers everywhere. He once engaged in learned discussion with Sima Hui. He is Xu Shu of Yingchuan, whose courtesy name is Yuanzhi. ‘Shan Fu’ is merely an assumed name.” Cao Cao asked, “How does Xu Shu’s ability compare with yours?” Cheng Yu replied, “His ability is ten times mine.” Cao Cao said, “What a pity that so worthy a man has gone over to Liu Bei! Liu Bei now has his wings. What are we to do?” Cheng Yu said, “Though Xu Shu is with him, if you wish to employ the man, Prime Minister, it will not be difficult to summon him here.” Cao Cao asked, “How can we make him come over to us?” Cheng Yu replied, “Xu Shu is a most filial man. He lost his father when young and has only his aged mother at home. His younger brother Xu Kang is now dead, so there is no one to attend and support her. You may send someone to lure his mother to Xuchang and have her write a letter summoning her son. Then Xu Shu is certain to come.”

p.src: Cao Cao was delighted and sent men out that very night to fetch Xu Shu’s mother. Within a day she was brought to him. Cao Cao treated her generously and said, “I have heard that your worthy son Xu Yuanzhi is an extraordinary talent under heaven. He is now in Xinye, assisting the traitor Liu Bei and rebelling against the imperial court. It is just as if a beautiful jade had fallen into the mire—a truly regrettable thing. I must now trouble you, honored mother, to write a letter calling him back to the capital of Xu. I shall recommend him before the Emperor, and he will certainly receive a rich reward.”

p.src: Cao Cao then ordered his attendants to bring the Four Treasures of the Study and told Xu Shu’s mother to write a letter. Xu Shu’s mother asked, “What kind of man is Liu Bei?” Cao Cao replied, “He is a petty fellow from Pei Commandery who falsely styles himself Imperial Uncle. He is utterly devoid of good faith—the sort of man who appears a gentleman without but is a villain within.” Xu Shu’s mother cried sternly, “How can you utter such monstrous lies! I have long heard that Xuande is descended from Prince Jing of Zhongshan, a distant great-grandson of Emperor Jing of Han; that he humbles himself before men of worth, receives others with courtesy and modesty, and has long been renowned for benevolence. Children and old men, shepherd boys and woodcutters throughout the realm all know his name. He is truly a hero of this age. In assisting him, my son has found the lord he ought to serve. Though you bear the title of Chancellor of Han, you are in truth a traitor to Han; yet you call Xuande a rebel and seek to make my son forsake the light for darkness. Are you not ashamed of yourself?”

p.src: With that, she seized a stone inkstone and hurled it at Cao Cao. Cao Cao flew into a rage and ordered his guards to drag her out and behead her. Cheng Yu hastily stopped him. He entered and remonstrated with Cao Cao: “Xu Shu’s mother deliberately provoked Your Excellency because she seeks death. If Your Excellency kills her, you will incur a reputation for injustice while perfecting her virtuous name. Once his mother is dead, Xu Shu will surely devote himself utterly to aiding Liu Bei and avenging her. Better to keep her alive, leaving Xu Shu divided in body and mind; then even if he aids Liu Bei, he will not exert himself fully. Moreover, so long as his mother remains here, I have a plan to lure Xu Shu here to serve Your Excellency.”

p.src: Cao Cao agreed and spared Xu Shu’s mother, placing her in separate quarters where she was cared for. Cheng Yu visited her daily, falsely claiming that he and Xu Shu had once sworn brotherhood, and treated her as though she were his own mother; whenever he sent her gifts, he always enclosed a note in his own hand. Xu Shu’s mother therefore replied with handwritten notes of her own. Having thus obtained samples of her handwriting, Cheng Yu imitated her script and forged a family letter. He dispatched a trusted man with it straight to Xinye County to inquire after Shan Fu’s camp. The soldiers conducted the man to Xu Shu. When Xu Shu learned that a letter had come from his mother, he hurriedly summoned the messenger and questioned him. The man said, “I am a servant from your household. p.src: When Xu Shu had finished reading, tears gushed from his eyes. Carrying the letter, he went to Xuande and said, “I am in truth Xu Shu of Yingchuan, courtesy name Yuanzhi; because I was fleeing calamity, I changed my name to Shan Fu. Earlier, hearing that Liu Jingsheng welcomed men of worth and talent, I went especially to see him. But after discussing affairs with him, I realized that he was a man of no use. I wrote him a letter of farewell, then traveled by night to Master Water Mirror’s estate and told him what had happened. Water Mirror sternly reproached me for failing to recognize a worthy lord, saying, ‘Liu, Governor of Yuzhou, is here. Why do you not serve him?’ I therefore feigned madness and sang in the marketplace, hoping to attract Your Lordship’s notice. Happily, you did not disdain me, but at once entrusted me with great responsibility. But alas, through Cao Cao’s treacherous scheme my aged mother has now been lured to Xuchang and imprisoned, and they are about to harm her. She has summoned me in a letter written by her own hand; I cannot refuse to go. It is not that I do not wish to labor like a dog or horse in Your Lordship’s service and repay your kindness; but with my beloved mother held captive, I cannot devote my full strength to you. I must now take my leave and return home; may we meet again hereafter.”

p.src: Hearing this, Xuande wept bitterly and said, “The bond between mother and son is ordained by Heaven. Yuanzhi, do not let concern for me detain you. After you have been reunited with the old lady, perhaps I may once more receive your instruction.” Xu Shu bowed in gratitude and prepared to depart. Xuande said, “I beg you to remain with us for one more night. Tomorrow we shall give you a farewell banquet.” Sun Qian privately said to Xuande, “Yuanzhi is an extraordinary talent without equal under Heaven. Having long resided in Xinye, he knows all the strengths and weaknesses of our army. If we now let him return to Cao Cao, Cao will surely place him in a position of great trust, and we shall be in danger. My lord should insist that he remain and by no means let him go. When Cao Cao sees that Yuanzhi has not come, he will surely behead his mother. When Yuanzhi learns of her death, he will surely avenge his mother and devote all his strength to attacking Cao Cao.” Xuande said, “That cannot be done. To cause a man’s mother to be killed and then employ her son would be inhumane; to keep him here and prevent him from going, thereby severing the bond between mother and son, would be unrighteous. I would rather die than commit an act devoid of benevolence and righteousness.” All who heard him were moved and sighed in admiration. Xuande invited Xu Shu to drink, but Xu Shu said, “Now that I have learned my aged mother is imprisoned, even liquid gold and jade could not pass my throat.” Xuande replied, “When I heard that you were leaving, it was as though I had lost both arms. Even dragon’s liver and phoenix marrow would have no savor for me.”

p.src: The two sat facing one another and wept as they waited for dawn. The officers had already prepared a farewell banquet outside the city walls. Xuande and Xu Shu rode side by side out of the city. Reaching the roadside pavilion, they dismounted to bid farewell. Raising his cup, Xuande said to Xu Shu, “My fortune is meager and our affinity too slight, so I cannot keep you beside me. I hope you will serve your new lord well and win achievement and renown.” Xu Shu wept and said, “My talents are slight and my wisdom shallow, yet Your Lordship honored me with great responsibility. That I must now unhappily leave you midway is solely because of my aged mother. Even if Cao Cao tries to compel me, I shall never devise a single stratagem for him as long as I live.” Xuande said, “Once you are gone, I too shall withdraw far away into the mountains and forests.” Xu Shu replied, “In joining Your Lordship to pursue the enterprise of kingship and hegemony, I relied upon the counsel held within this heart of mine. Now, because of my aged mother, my heart is in turmoil. Even if I remained here, I would be of no use to your cause. Your Lordship should seek another great worthy to assist you in pursuing the grand enterprise. Why lose heart so readily?” Xuande said, “Among all the worthies under Heaven, none surpasses you.” Xu Shu replied, “I am but useless timber, a man of mediocre ability. How could I deserve such high praise?” At the moment of parting, he turned again to the officers and said, “I pray that you gentlemen serve Your Lordship well, so that your names may be inscribed upon bamboo and silk and your achievements recorded in history. By no means imitate my failure to remain steadfast to the end.” Every one of the officers was overcome with sorrow. Unable to bear the parting, Xuande accompanied him for another stage of the road. Then he accompanied him for yet another stage. Xu Shu took leave of him, saying, “Your Lordship need not trouble yourself to accompany me farther. Here I must bid you farewell.” Still on horseback, Xuande clasped Xu Shu’s hand and said, “Once you depart, we shall be separated at opposite ends of the heavens. Who knows on what day we may meet again!” As he finished speaking, tears fell like rain. Xu Shu too wept as he took his leave.

p.src: Xuande halted his horse beside the woods and watched Xu Shu ride hurriedly away with his attendants. Xuande wept, “Yuanzhi is gone! What am I to do?” He gazed after him through gathering tears, until a grove of trees blocked his view. Pointing with his whip, Xuande said, “I want every tree in this place cut down.” The others asked why. Xuande replied, “Because they obstruct my eyes from watching Xu Yuanzhi.”

p.src: As he continued gazing, he suddenly saw Xu Shu spur his horse and return. Xuande said, “Yuanzhi has returned—can it be that he no longer means to leave?” Delighted, he spurred forward to meet him and asked, “Sir, now that you have returned, surely you have some purpose in mind?” Xu Shu reined in his horse and said to Xuande, “My thoughts were in such turmoil that I forgot to tell you one thing. There is an extraordinary man hereabouts, living at Longzhong, twenty li outside Xiangyang. Why does Your Lordship not seek him out?” Xuande said, “May I trouble you, Yuanzhi, to invite him here to meet me?” Xu Shu replied, “This is not a man who can be summoned into service. Your Lordship must go and seek him in person. If you obtain this man, it will be no different from the Zhou gaining Lü Wang or the Han gaining Zhang Liang.” Xuande asked, “How do this man’s talent and virtue compare with yours?” Xu Shu replied, “To compare me with him would be like setting a worn-out nag beside a qilin, or matching a jackdaw with a luan and phoenix. He has often compared himself to Guan Zhong and Yue Yi; but in my judgment, even Guan Zhong and Yue Yi could scarcely equal him. He possesses the talent to order Heaven and weave the Earth; there is surely no other man like him under Heaven.”

p.src: Xuande said joyfully, “I should like to hear this man’s name.” Xu Shu said, “This man is a native of Yangdu in Langya. His compound surname is Zhuge, his given name is Liang, and his courtesy name is Kongming. He is a descendant of Zhuge Feng, who served the Han as Colonel Director of Retainers. His father, Zhuge Gui, whose courtesy name was Zigong, served as assistant administrator of Taishan Commandery and died young. Liang then followed his uncle, Zhuge Xuan. Xuan had an old friendship with Liu Jingsheng of Jingzhou, so he went to seek refuge with him and settled his household in Xiangyang. After Xuan died, Liang and his younger brother Zhuge Jun tilled the fields themselves in Nanyang. He was fond of chanting the ‘Liangfu Song.’ There was a ridge where he lived called Sleeping Dragon Ridge, and so he styled himself Master Sleeping Dragon. This man is a genius without equal in the age. You should lose no time in condescending to visit him, my lord. If he consents to assist you, why should you fear that the realm cannot be pacified?” Xuande said, “Master Water Mirror once told me, ‘Of Sleeping Dragon and Young Phoenix, gain either one and you can bring peace to the realm.’ Can those he spoke of be none other than this Sleeping Dragon and Young Phoenix?” Xu Shu said, “Young Phoenix is Pang Tong of Xiangyang. Sleeping Dragon is none other than Zhuge Kongming.” Xuande leapt with delight and said, “Only today have I learned the meaning of the words ‘Sleeping Dragon and Young Phoenix.’ Who would have thought that so great a worthy was close at hand? p.src: Having recommended Kongming, Xu Shu bade Xuande farewell once more, spurred his horse, and departed. On hearing Xu Shu’s words, Xuande at last understood what Sima Decao had told him. Like a drunkard newly sobered, like a dreamer just awakened, he led his generals back to Xinye, prepared lavish gifts, and set out with Guan Yu and Zhang Fei for Nanyang to invite Kongming to join him.

p.src: Now after taking leave of Xuande, Xu Shu was moved by the affection with which Xuande had sought to keep him and feared that Kongming might refuse to leave his retreat and lend him aid. He therefore rode straight to the foot of Sleeping Dragon Ridge and entered the thatched cottage to see Kongming. Kongming asked why he had come. Xu Shu said, “I had wished to serve Liu, Governor of Yuzhou, but my aged mother was taken prisoner by Cao Cao, who sent me a letter summoning me. I had no choice but to leave Liu and go to her. Before departing, I recommended you to Xuande. Xuande will come this very day to pay his respects. I pray you do not turn him away, but display the great talents of your lifetime and lend him your aid. Nothing could be more fortunate.”
